cells.tense: The many possible feelings are here and the direction is not yet chosen
cells.act: count it out and read what the numbers show
cells.ask: Count what you're carrying and what each direction would need, before committing. Write the numbers down, then read what they show before you decide.
cells.core:
You hold a lot open when a direction has to be chosen. Several feelings about one situation can all be true at once, and you don't pretend otherwise. That range gives whatever you settle on weight behind it. Nothing gets thrown out before it has been looked at, and you are slow to close a road you might want later.

Before the next decision, count what is actually here: how many real options, what each would ask of you, what each would cost. Write the numbers plainly. You don't need the whole field mapped before you can see which rows point the same way. What is already here is enough to choose from, and counting will show you which direction has weight and which one is only loud.
cells.sheetLine: You hold every possibility open before you pick one.
cells.place: At the fork in the road, where direction is chosen once and not again

cells.tense: Every road will have to stay open, or the one taken will feel like a loss
cells.ask: Take one commitment you've already made and hold it this week exactly as it stands — no revisions, no new options let in.
cells.core:
When a direction is chosen, the roads you didn't take keep their pull, and the way you pay that cost is to postpone committing. The plan stays provisional, the promise stays adjustable, the shape you said you would give something keeps getting reopened in case a better version arrives. What has been decided is real, but it is stored as still-changing, so what your hands make doesn't get to stay made.

Let one commitment keep its shape. Take something you have already set in motion and hold it, this week, as it stands — no revisions, no letting a fresh option in to soften it. A week is not forever. What survives one unchanged week was decided; what doesn't was not quite on the road yet.
cells.sheetLine: You keep it open so the choice doesn't have to be final.

cells.tense: The many possible feelings were once here and the road is not being walked
cells.act: put the problem down and take a walk with nothing to solve
cells.ask: Leave the question of where you're headed until tomorrow and go outside with nothing to solve for half an hour.
cells.core:
There used to be a person here who could feel the whole range at once and still choose. That part has gone quiet. The feeling is still available — several ways at once, all honest — but the hand that would pick one has stopped reaching. You wait for a certainty strong enough to settle it, and the waiting passes for thinking. The roads are all still where they were, and none of them is being walked.

Put the problem down for one evening and go outside with nothing to solve. Not to feel better, not to decide — to let the mind stop calibrating for a while. What settles when you stop working it is usually the answer you were going to reach anyway, minus the friction. The fork is not going anywhere, and neither is the one who has to walk it.
cells.sheetLine: The roads are all still open and none is being taken.

cells.tense: The picking is happening and the picker is filing it under circumstance
cells.act: work the pattern through to its logic
cells.ask: Write one line about what you actually do when several feelings are on the table at once. Mine runs the pattern. No verdict.
cells.core:
You are already choosing, steadily, and the choice gets charged to mood or timing or what other people needed that week. You read the table, you price the options, you take the road that keeps the most options warm — then you describe it as having gone wherever it went. The range you have is real. So is the hand that narrows it, and that hand works with no name on the work.

Take one stretch of it and work it out plainly. What do you do when several feelings about one thing are live? Write the pattern in a single line, as it actually runs, and read it back. There is no verdict in this and nothing to fix. The point is only that the pattern has an author, and reading your own line back is how the author gets named.

attempts.check: The record gives me the card as gathering emotional possibilities, the seat as choosing direction, and the medicine's own acts; it does not say the person keeps a storehouse, that feeling is grain, or that anything is being mislabeled as mood. A reader could reasonably say the many possibilities are just a wide field of attention, not a granary, and that counting what you carry is a strategy rather than a gift. The asks survive being wrong because counting, finishing one thing, walking with nothing to solve, and writing a pattern are each useful on their own whether or not the read lands. The sentence that serves me more than them is the one about the hand being left off the books, which assigns them an inner accounting they never reported.
